title: Wave equation v = fλ
examples: What is the difference between frequency and wavelength?
How do I calculate the speed of a wave?
If I know the frequency and speed, can I find the wavelength?

explain.say: Today we are learning about waves and their properties.
First we look at frequency. Frequency measures how many waves pass a point.
Next we look at wavelength. Wavelength is the distance for one full wave cycle.
The period is the time taken for one complete wave cycle to pass by.
The relationship between these three is very important to remember.
For a real-life example, think about a wave on a rope.

faq.q: What is the relationship between period and frequency?
faq.a: The period is the reciprocal of the frequency. This means they are inversely related.
asks: How do I switch between T and f?

faq.q: Does the speed of a wave change if I change its frequency?
faq.a: The speed of the wave only changes if the medium it travels through changes. Frequency and wavelength change, but speed stays constant.
asks: Can I change the speed by changing frequency?
Is the speed always constant for a wave?

faq.q: What are the units I must use for these calculations?
faq.a: Speed is usually meters per second, frequency is Hertz or cycles per second, and wavelength is meters.
asks: What units for v, f, and λ?
Do I use meters or centimeters for wavelength?

faq.q: If I know the speed and frequency, how do I find the wavelength?
faq.a: You rearrange the formula to solve for wavelength. You divide the speed by the frequency.
asks: How do I find λ if I have v and f?
What is the formula for λ?

faq.q: Is the wave speed always the same for all waves?
faq.a: No, the speed depends on the material or medium the wave is traveling through. Sound travels faster in solids than in air.
asks: Does the medium affect wave speed?
Why does sound travel differently in water?

facts: Frequency is measured in Hertz, which means cycles per second.
Wavelength is the distance between two consecutive points on a wave.
The relationship connecting speed, frequency, and wavelength is v equals f times λ.
The period (T) is the reciprocal of the frequency (f), so T equals one divided by f.

quiz.say: A wave has a frequency of ten Hertz and a wavelength of two meters. What is its speed?
quiz.why: You multiply the frequency, ten, by the wavelength, two, to get twenty meters per second.

wrong.0: You might divide the wavelength by the frequency, reversing the formula.
wrong.2: You might divide the values, which is incorrect for this formula.
wrong.3: You might only use the frequency value, ignoring the wavelength.

quiz.say: If the period of a wave is one-half a second, what is its frequency?
quiz.why: Frequency is the reciprocal of the period. One divided by one-half gives two.

wrong.0: You might assume the period and frequency are equal.
wrong.2: You might mistake the period for the frequency directly.
wrong.3: While mathematically correct, the standard unit is just the number, Hertz.

quiz.say: A wave travels at thirty meters per second and has a frequency of five Hertz. What is its wavelength?
quiz.why: To find the wavelength, you divide the speed, thirty, by the frequency, five.

wrong.0: You might write the calculation but forget to state the final unit.
wrong.1: You might incorrectly divide the frequency by the speed.
wrong.3: You might multiply the speed by the frequency, which is incorrect.
